Definition: from G1 (as a particle of union) and G3956; absolutely all or (singular) every one:--all (things), every (one), whole.
BiblicalUsage: Hapas means all, absolutely all, with nothing left out, and Luke loves the word. In Acts 2:44 all that believed were together and had all things common, in Acts 4:31 they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, in Luke 19:37 the whole multitude began to praise God, and in Matthew 6:32 Jesus says the Father knows we have need of all these things.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word leaves me nowhere to hide: all believed, all were filled, all praised. The gospel is not a partial thing, and neither is the Father's care.
